name: .NET · 4 YOE Path
desc: Built from the deep-research reports and 4 YOE handbook: trade-offs, ASP.NET, EF/SQL, security, messaging, memory diagnostics, CQRS, SCIM, and system-design drills interviewers actually ask around 4 years experience.
tip: At 4 YOE, lead with trade-offs and production stories. Depth beats buzzwords — explain why you chose async, a cache TTL, or an isolation level.
setup:
Cadence: Week 1 — C#/async/DI/ASP.NET/EF.
Week 2 — Security, messaging, caching, observability, memory/GC + 3 designs.
Week 3 — CQRS, SCIM/OAuth2, Mock interviews, resume deep-dives, STAR stories.

r: RCSI vs locks; when you need a transaction
Avoid dual-write between DB and bus
dotnet-dump/gcdump to diagnose leaks; LOH/POH bounds
In-process mediator vs out-of-process event bus

parts.title: How 4 YOE interviews work + roadmap
parts.summary: Interviewers at ~4 years expect ownership of a vertical slice, production debugging, and clear trade-offs — not Staff-level CLR trivia. Typical loop: screen → t…

parts.title: C# essentials — IEnumerable, boxing, Span, records
parts.summary: Language questions at 4 YOE test whether you know where work runs (memory vs SQL) and allocation cost — not trivia for its own sake.

parts.title: Async — state machine, ValueTask, deadlocks, starvation
parts.summary: `async` builds a state machine; it does not spawn a thread. At 4 YOE you must diagnose deadlocks and thread-pool starvation in production language.

parts.title: DI lifetimes, HttpClient, Options pattern
parts.summary: Captive dependencies and socket exhaustion are classic 4 YOE gotchas. Know Transient/Scoped/Singleton cold.

parts.title: ASP.NET Core — Kestrel, middleware, Minimal vs MVC
parts.summary: Know the request path: Kestrel → middleware → endpoint. Wrong middleware order causes 'auth never runs' bugs.

parts.title: API design — REST, versioning, idempotency, rate limits
parts.summary: Design questions at 4 YOE are about practical APIs: versioning, pagination, idempotency keys, and status codes — not HATEOAS purity contests.

parts.title: EF Core & SQL — N+1, indexes, AsNoTracking
parts.summary: Data access is where mid-senior candidates separate themselves: N+1, plans, and read vs write patterns.

parts.title: Transactions, isolation, concurrency, soft delete
parts.summary: Isolation levels and optimistic concurrency are favorite 4 YOE topics — especially RCSI vs locking.

parts.title: Security — OAuth2/PKCE, JWT, OWASP
parts.summary: Be fluent in auth code + PKCE, JWT validation claims, and the OWASP issues that hit .NET APIs.

parts.title: Messaging — RabbitMQ vs Kafka, outbox, saga
parts.summary: Know when to pick a broker, what partitions mean, and how to avoid dual-write bugs.

parts.title: Observability & resilience — OTel, latency, Polly
parts.summary: Logs + metrics + traces, correlated by trace id. Plus timeouts, retries, and circuit breakers used correctly.

parts.title: Architecture — clean architecture, caching, microservices honesty
parts.summary: Defend layering choices. Don't propose microservices for a simple CRUD app — interviewers reward honesty.

parts.title: Cloud & DevOps — App Service vs AKS, CI/CD
parts.summary: At 4 YOE, compare hosting options and describe a safe deploy/rollback path.

parts.title: System design drills + behavioral finals
parts.summary: Practice mid-senior designs (~35 min): URL shortener, notifications, rate limiter, checkout. Close with STAR stories.

parts.title: Advanced Memory Diagnostics, GC Internals & Profiling
parts.summary: Production debugging at 4 YOE requires explaining Server vs Workstation GC, Gen 0/1/2, LOH/POH, memory leak diagnosis using dotnet-dump, dotnet-gcdump, and memo…

parts.title: CQRS, MediatR & Integration Event Patterns
parts.summary: Mid-senior roles test your understanding of separating reads from writes, pipeline behaviors, and reliable inter-service event communication.

parts.title: Enterprise Auth — OAuth2, SCIM 2.0, Rate Limiting & Token Security
parts.summary: Senior interviews for enterprise SaaS expect deep knowledge of identity provisioning (SCIM), OAuth2/OIDC token security, and API rate limiting.
